units.zh: 制可之。
units.en: The throne approved.
units.literal: The ordinance approved it.

units.zh: 帝怒，命宋州節度使元行欽率騎三千赴鄴都招撫，詔征諸道之師進討。
units.en: Cunxu sent Yuan Xingqin of Song with 3,000 horse to pacify Ye and ordered circuit armies to attack.
units.literal: The Emperor in rage ordered Songzhou military commissioner Yuan Xingqin to lead three thousand cavalry to Ye to pacify them, and issued an edict the various circuits' armies to advance for punishment.

units.zh: 辛丑，元行欽至鄴都，進攻南門，以詔書招諭城中，趙在禮獻羊酒勞軍，登城遙拜行欽曰：「將士經年離隔父母，不取敕旨歸寧，上貽聖憂，追悔何及！
units.en: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and used an edict to summon the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and bowed from the wall to Xingqin, saying, "The soldiers have been separated from their parents for years; by returning home without edict, they have burdened the sage with worry. What regret can suffice!
units.literal: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and with an edict summoned the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and from the wall bowed distantly to Xingqin, saying, "The troops were separated from parents for years and, not taking the edict to return home, burdened the sage—what regret can suffice!

units.zh: 丁未，鄴都行營招撫使元行欽率諸道之師再攻鄴都。
units.en: On dingwei Yuan Xingqin led circuit armies against Ye again.
units.literal: On dingwei Ye campaign pacification commissioner Yuan Xingqin led the various circuits' armies to attack Ye again.

units.zh: 行欽曰：「上以汝輩有社稷功，必行赦宥。」
units.en: Xingqin said, "Because you have merit for the altars of state, the sovereign will surely grant pardon."
units.literal: Xingqin said, "The sovereign, because you have merit for the altars of state, will surely grant pardon."

units.zh: 行欽以聞，帝怒曰：「收城之日，勿遺噍類！」
units.en: Cunxu, told, raged: "When the city falls, spare none!"
units.literal: Xingqin reported it; the Emperor in rage said, "On the day the city is taken, leave no mouth!"

units.zh: 壬寅，行欽自鄴退軍，保澶州。
units.en: On renyin Xingqin withdrew to Chan.
units.literal: On renyin Xingqin withdrew from Ye and held Chanzhou.

units.zh: 少為唐宰臣崔魏公家臣，後因亂，客於蒲州。
units.en: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister, the Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.
units.literal: In youth he served as a household retainer of the Tang chief minister Duke of Wei surnamed Cui; later, amid the turmoil, he sojourned in Puzhou.

units.zh: 會於頔、杜黃裳家私事發，連逮鑒虛下獄。
units.en: When private scandals at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.
units.literal: When private affairs at the homes of Yu Di and Du Huangshang came to light, Jianxu was implicated and imprisoned.

units.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽南院使、判內侍省、兼內局、特進、左監門將軍同正李紹宏為右領軍衛上將軍。
units.en: On xinmao Li Shaohong—Southern Secretariat attendant, Inner Palace overseer, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general—became senior general of the Right Guard.
units.literal: On xinmao, Palace Attendant of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, overseer of the Inner Palace, concurrent Inner Bureau, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general of the same rank Li Shaohong was made senior general of the Right Imperial Guard.

units.zh: 是時梁有敬翔，燕有馬鬱，華州有李巨川，荊南有鄭準，
units.en: Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,
units.literal: At that time Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua Prefecture had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,

units.zh: 燕人馬鬱，有盛名於鄉里，而緘素以吏職事鬱。
units.en: Ma Yu of Yan enjoyed great local fame, though Jian had long served him in a clerk's capacity.
units.literal: Ma Yu of Yan had great fame in his home district, while Jian had long served Yu in a clerk's post.

units.zh: 及鬱在太原，謂緘曰：「公在此作文士，所謂避風之鳥，受賜於魯人也。」
units.en: When Yu came to Taiyuan he told Jian, "You play the literary man here—the bird that flees the storm and finds shelter with a stranger in Lu."
units.literal: When Yu was at Taiyuan he said to Jian: "You serve here as a literary man—the so-called bird that flees the wind and receives favor from the man of Lu."

units.zh: 自廣明大亂之後，諸侯割據方面，競延名士，以掌書檄。
units.en: After the great disorders of the Guangming reign, regional lords carved up the empire and competed to recruit famous scholars to draft their letters and battle proclamations.
units.literal: From after the great disorder of the Guangming era, feudal lords held regions by force and vied to summon famous scholars to manage letters and proclamations.

units.zh: 十年，從征幽州，既獲仁恭父子，莊宗命緘為露布，觀其旨趣。
units.en: In the tenth year he marched on Youzhou; after Rengong and his sons were taken, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to see where his loyalties lay.
units.literal: In the tenth year he followed the campaign against Youzhou; after Rengong father and son were captured, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Jian to draft the victory bulletin to observe his intent.

units.zh: 每於公宴，但呼王緘而已。
units.en: At every public feast he would call only "Wang Jian" and use no other name for him.
units.literal: At every public banquet he would only call out "Wang Jian" and nothing more.

units.zh: 本姓康，幼閹，為內常侍張泰養子。
units.en: Born Kang, he was castrated young and raised by the inner attendant Zhang Tai.
units.literal: His original surname was Kang; castrated in youth, he was adopted by the Inner Regular Attendant Zhang Tai.

units.zh: 張承業，字繼元，唐僖宗時宦者也。
units.en: Zhang Chengye, courtesy name Jiyuan, served as a palace eunuch under Tang Xizong.
units.literal: Zhang Chengye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was a eunuch in the time of Emperor Xizong of Tang.

units.zh: 公叔既死，公孫鞅聞秦孝公下令國中求賢者，將修繆公之業，東復侵地，乃遂西入秦，因孝公寵臣景監以求見孝公。
units.en: After Gongshu's death, Gongsun Yang learned that Duke Xiao of Qin had issued an edict throughout his realm seeking talented men. The duke intended to revive Duke Mu's legacy and recover territories lost to the east. Yang traveled west to Qin and, through the duke's favored minister Jing Jian, sought an audience with Duke Xiao.
units.literal: Gongshu having died, Gongsun Yang heard that Duke Xiao of Qin had issued an edict throughout the state seeking worthy men, intending to revive Duke Mu's achievements and eastward recover lost territories, so he went west to Qin, through Duke Xiao's favored minister Jing Jian to seek audience with Duke Xiao.

units.zh: 罷而孝公怒景監曰：「子之客妄人耳，安足用邪！」
units.en: After the audience ended, Duke Xiao angrily rebuked Jing Jian, saying, "Your guest is nothing but a charlatan! How could he possibly be of use?"
units.literal: Retiring, Duke Xiao angrily rebuked Jing Jian: 'Your guest is a charlatan, how can he be employed!'

units.zh: 今君之見秦王也，因嬖人景監以為主，非所以為名也。
units.en: Now Your Lordship obtained an audience with the King of Qin through the patronage of the favored minister Jing Jian. That is not the way to establish a name.
units.literal: Now Your Lordship gained audience with the King of Qin through the favored minister Jing Jian as sponsor; this is not the way to establish a reputation.

units.zh: 景監以讓衛鞅。
units.en: Jing Jian conveyed this rebuke to Wei Yang.
units.literal: Jing Jian conveyed this criticism to Wei Yang.

units.zh: 罷而孝公復讓景監，景監亦讓鞅。
units.en: After the audience ended, Duke Xiao again rebuked Jing Jian, who in turn rebuked Yang.
units.literal: After the audience, Duke Xiao again scolded Jing Jian, who in turn scolded Yang.

units.zh: 孝公謂景監曰：「汝客善，可與語矣。」
units.en: Duke Xiao told Jing Jian, "Your guest is impressive—one can actually hold a conversation with him."
units.literal: Duke Xiao told Jing Jian: 'Your guest is good, one can converse with him.'

units.zh: 景監曰：「子何以中吾君？
units.en: Jing Jian asked, "How did you manage to please our lord?
units.literal: Jing Jian said: 'How did you hit upon our lord's pleasure?

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德三年春三月，晉潞州節度留後李繼韜遣使以城歸順。
units.en: In the third month of Longde 3 Li Jiyao of Luzhou offered the city to Liang.
units.literal: In the third month of spring of Longde 3, Jin Luzhou military retention commissioner Li Jiyao sent envoys offering the city in submission.

units.zh: 制以郢王友圭充控鶴指揮使，諸軍都虞候閻寶為御營使。
units.en: Prince of Ying Yougui was made Crane-Control commander and Yan Bao, army chief of staff, imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: An edict made Prince of Ying Yougui Crane-Control commander and army chief of staff Yan Bao imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 初，崇韜與李紹宏同為內職，及莊宗即位，崇韜以紹宏素在己上，舊人難製，即奏澤潞監軍張居翰同掌樞密，以紹宏為宣徽使。
units.en: Earlier, Guo Chongtao and Li Shaohong had both served in the inner administration. After Zhuangzong's accession, Guo Chongtao—finding that Li Shaohong had always outranked him and that an old associate was difficult to manage—petitioned to have Zhang Juhán, military commissioner of Ze and Lu, share control of Military Affairs, while appointing Li Shaohong Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: Initially Guo Chongtao and Li Shaohong both held inner-court posts. When Zhuangzong took the throne, Guo Chongtao, because Li Shaohong had long ranked above him and old colleagues were hard to control, memorialized to have Zhang Juhán, military overseer of Ze and Lu, share charge of Military Affairs, and made Li Shaohong Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 時潞王鎮鳳翔，與之鄰境，及潞王不稟朝旨，致書於秦、涇、雍、梁、邠諸帥，言：「賊臣亂政，屬先帝疾篤，謀害秦王，迎立嗣君，自擅權柄，以致殘害骨肉，搖動藩垣。
units.en: The Prince of Lu held Fengxiang on Sitong's border. When he defied the court he wrote the governors of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin: "Wicked ministers have thrown the government into chaos. As the late emperor lay dying they plotted against the Prince of Qin, installed a puppet heir, and seized power for themselves, wounding the imperial family and unsettling the frontiers.
units.literal: At that time the Prince of Lu garrisoned Fengxiang, neighboring his territory; when the Prince of Lu did not obey court orders he sent letters to the commanders of Qin, Jing, Yong, Liang, and Bin, stating, "Traitorous ministers have disorderly government; when the late emperor was gravely ill they plotted to harm the Prince of Qin, welcomed and set up the heir, and on their own grasped power, causing harm to the imperial kin and shaking the frontier screens.

units.zh: 己酉，北京奏，光祿卿致仕周元豹卒。
units.en: On jiyou the Northern Capital reported the death of Zhou Yuanbao, former Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs.
units.literal: On jiyou, Beijing reported that Zhou Yuanbao, retired Director of the Directorate of Foodstuffs, had died.

units.zh: 王淑妃曰：「從榮在此。」
units.en: Consort Wang Shufei said, "Congrong is here."
units.literal: Consort Wang Shufei said: "Congrong is here."

units.zh: 明宗命王淑妃母之，嘗謂左右曰：「惟此兒生於皇宮，故尤所鍾愛。」
units.en: Mingzong appointed Consort Wang Shufei as his foster mother and once told his attendants, "Only this child was born in the palace itself, and so I cherish him above all."
units.literal: Emperor Mingzong ordered Consort Wang Shufei to be his foster mother and once said to those around him: "Only this child was born within the imperial palace, and so I especially cherish him."

units.zh: 〈（《五代史闕文》：漢高祖自太原起軍建號，至洛陽，會郭從義先入京師，受密旨殺王淑妃與許王從益。
units.en: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties records that Gaozu of Han raised his army at Taiyuan and established his reign. Reaching Luoyang, he found Guo Congyi already in the capital with a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.
units.literal: (Lost Writings of the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu of Han raised an army at Taiyuan and established his reign; reaching Luoyang, he met Guo Congyi, who had entered the capital first and received a secret order to kill Consort Wang Shufei and Prince Xu Congyi.

units.zh: 淑妃臨刑號泣曰：「吾家子母何罪，吾既為契丹所立，非敢與人爭國，何不且留吾兒，每年寒食，使持一盂飯灑明宗陵寢。」
units.en: Facing execution the consort wept aloud, "What crime have mother and son committed? The Khitan installed me; I never sought to contend for the realm. Why not spare my son, so that each Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to Mingzong's tomb?"
units.literal: Facing execution the consort wept aloud: "What crime have my household's mother and son committed? I was installed by the Khitan and did not dare contend for the realm with others—why not at least spare my son, so that each year at Cold Food he may bring one bowl of rice to pour at Emperor Mingzong's tomb?"

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒·明宗紀》云：己丑，大漸，秦王從榮入問疾，帝俯首不能舉。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror, annals of Mingzong, records that on jichou the emperor's illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong came to inquire after him, but the emperor could only bow his head and could not lift it.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror·Annals of Mingzong states: On jichou the illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong entered to inquire after the emperor's health; the emperor bowed his head and could not raise it.

units.zh: 會契丹主死，其汴州節度使蕭翰謀歸北地，慮中原無主，軍民大亂，則己亦不得按轡徐歸矣；
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north. He feared that with no ruler in the Central Plains and army and people in chaos, he himself could not withdraw at leisure;
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north and feared that with no ruler in central China and army and people in great disorder, he himself would be unable to rein in his horse and withdraw at leisure;

units.zh: 自貞簡太后、韓德妃、伊淑妃及諸公子在晉陽者，承業一切以法繩之，權貴皆斂手畏承業。
units.en: Empress Dowager Zhenjian, the consorts Hande and Yishu, the princes at Jinyang—Chengye held them all to the law, and the great families learned to fear him.
units.literal: From Empress Dowager Zhenjian, Consort Hande, Consort Yishu, and all the princes at Jinyang, Chengye bound every one by law; the powerful all shrank back in fear of him.

units.zh: 元行欽請車駕幸汴州，帝將發京師，遣中官向延嗣馳詔所在誅蜀主王衍，仍夷其族。
units.en: Yuan Xingqin asked Cunxu to go to Bian; as he was about to leave the capital he sent Xiang Yansi with a flying edict to execute Wang Yan and exterminate his clan.
units.literal: Yuan Xingqin asked that the imperial carriage go to Bianzhou; the Emperor was about to set out from the capital and sent a palace official, Xiang Yansi, with a flying edict to the place to execute Shu ruler Wang Yan and still exterminate his clan.

units.zh: 莊宗常兄事承業，歲時升堂拜母，甚親重之。
units.en: Zhuangzong treated him like an elder brother, visiting each year to bow to his mother, and held him in the highest regard.
units.literal: Zhuangzong always treated Chengye as an elder brother; each year he went up to the hall to bow to Chengye’s mother and held him in great affection.

units.zh: 自高祖初入長安，開大丞相府，下令置生員，自京師至於州縣皆有數。
units.en: When Gaozu first entered Chang'an and opened the Grand Chancellor's Office, he ordered student quotas established at every level from the capital down to prefectures and counties.
units.literal: From the time Gaozu first entered Chang'an and opened the Grand Chancellor's Office, he issued orders to establish student quotas, with fixed numbers from the capital down to prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 既即位，又詔秘書外省別立小學，以教宗室子孫及功臣子弟。
units.en: After his enthronement, he also ordered a separate elementary school outside the Secretariat to educate imperial clan descendants and sons of meritorious officials.
units.literal: After he took the throne, he also ordered a separate elementary school established outside the Secretariat to teach imperial clan descendants and sons of meritorious officials.

units.zh: 其後又詔諸州明經、秀才、俊士、進士明于理體為鄉里稱者，縣考試，州長重覆，歲隨方物入貢；
units.en: He later ordered that throughout the empire, candidates in Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi who showed mastery of principle and were acclaimed locally should be examined by their county, re-examined by the prefect, and sent annually to court with local tribute;
units.literal: Later he also ordered that in all prefectures those in Mingjing, Xiucai, Junshi, and Jinshi who were clear in principle and structure and acclaimed in their districts should be examined by the county, re-examined by the prefect, and each year sent in tribute with local products;

units.zh: 至巷伯詩列於《雅》，勃貂功著於晉，雖忠於所事，而非其職矣。
units.en: Later the "Palace Steward" ode entered the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao won fame in Jin—loyal to their masters, perhaps, but already acting outside their proper charge.
units.literal: By the time the Palace Steward ode was placed among the Greater Odes, and Bo Diao's achievements were celebrated in Jin, though loyal to those they served, this was no longer their proper office.

units.zh: 《周禮》，寺人掌中門之禁。
units.en: The Rites of Zhou assign palace stewards to guard the inner gates.
units.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, palace stewards guard the inner gates.

units.zh: 張居翰，字德卿，故唐掖廷令張從玫之養子。
units.en: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, a former Tang director of the palace provision bureau.
units.literal: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, former Director of the Palace Provision Bureau under Tang.
